Reviewed all 6 walk-in sore-throat visits from today. Five had POSITIVE rapid strep antigen tests (pt-1003, pt-1017, pt-1021, pt-1023, pt-1030); pt-1026 was negative/viral, so no antibiotic was ordered for her.

Antibiotics ordered (all 10-day courses for GAS pharyngitis):
- pt-1003 (Maria Lopez, 1958): amoxicillin 500 mg BID. Only allergy is sulfonamide (rash) - no beta-lactam contraindication.
- pt-1017 (Maria Lopez, 1991): amoxicillin 500 mg BID. No allergies; tolerated amoxicillin in 2023.
- pt-1030 (Daniel King): amoxicillin 500 mg BID. No allergies or chronic conditions.
- pt-1021 (Jennifer Lee): cephalexin 500 mg BID. Documented amoxicillin allergy was a mild delayed maculopapular rash (non-IgE, no hives/angioedema/respiratory involvement), so a 1st-generation cephalosporin is appropriate rather than amoxicillin.
- pt-1023 (Elizabeth Martin): clindamycin 300 mg TID. A scanned outside record (Lakeside Urgent Care, 2015-06-02) documents anaphylaxis to penicillin VK in 2011 (throat tightness, wheezing, hives, epinephrine given) that had never been entered on her allergy list.

Chart update: added "Penicillin - anaphylaxis, high criticality" to pt-1023's allergy list with the source of the history, so future prescribers are warned. All beta-lactams were avoided for her.

Note also that two distinct patients are named Maria Lopez (pt-1003 and pt-1017) with different allergy profiles and different regimens — orders were placed by patient id.

Panel-wide apixaban review (30 patients). Six patients are on apixaban; five take it for nonvalvular AF (pt-1002, pt-1008, pt-1019, pt-1022, pt-1028). pt-1029 takes apixaban 5 mg BID for acute PE (no AF), so it was outside the scope and left unchanged.

Applied the FDA label rule for NVAF (2.5 mg BID if >=2 of: age >=80, weight <=60 kg, SCr >=1.5 mg/dL) using the most current chart data:

Changed:
- pt-1008 (Harold Bennett): 5 mg BID -> 2.5 mg BID. Age 81 and weight 58.2 kg (128.3 lb measured at the 2026-09-24 visit, documented in the progress note but not on the flowsheet - the 2026-09-28 pharmacy consult used the stale 63.5 kg value and concluded only 1 criterion was met). SCr 1.31. 2 of 3 criteria met.
- pt-1022 (William Turner): 2.5 mg BID -> 5 mg BID. Only SCr 1.61 meets a criterion (age 79, weight 81.6 kg). The original 2024 reduction was based on CKD 3b/age 77, which is not a label criterion; he was underdosed.
- pt-1028 (Charles Young): 5 mg BID -> 2.5 mg BID. Age 82 and SCr 1.63 (2026-09-15, up from 1.31 at initiation); weight 70.3 kg. 2 of 3 criteria met.

No change:
- pt-1002 (Linda Park): only weight 57.6 kg meets a criterion (age 60, SCr 1.18). 5 mg BID correct.
- pt-1019 (Lisa Thompson): only weight 57.8 kg meets a criterion (age 68); SCr 1.74 on 2026-08-18 was transient AKI from gastroenteritis, resolved to 0.86 on 2026-09-02. 5 mg BID correct.

No other medications were altered.
